newsitem.title: USA: Gateway's Waitt sees different vision at Compaq.
newsitem.headline: Gateway's Waitt sees different vision at Compaq.

text.p: Gateway 2000 CEO Ted Wiatt said his company's vision of doing business in the PC market was "a lot different" than that of its recent suitor, Compaq Computer Corp.

In a keynote presentation to a UK/U.S. Partners in Technology conference here, Wiatt outlined the company's emphasis on sharing common values and using teamwork to build computers to order to match customers' needs.
"We do business directly. Each customer is somewhat unique. We build the computer specifically for that customer," he said, noting it takes about three to four days to build and deliver the systems.
Wiatt said the company grew to a $5 billion in revenue largely by setting out "to help our customers manage the risk, manage the far of purchasing the technology".
He said companies will need to be able to change product pricing daily and create a new product nearly every day to accommodate rapid changes in businesses.
"Our most valuable assets are our relationships with customers, relationships with employees, and relationships with suppliers," he said.
Asked afterwards whether this vision contrasted with that of Compaq, he said it was "a lot different".
He declined to discuss reports about past takeover talks between Compaq and Gateway 2000.
Time Magazine reported Monday that Compaq and Gateway 2000 had nearly agreed to a virtually $7 billion merger last month but that Wiatt rejected it at the last moment.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Compaq has now decided to add 2,000 more people, partly in a bid to get closer to its customers, following the failed attempt to acquire Gateway 2000. ((sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau 415 846 5400))
